name: Dana P. Goldman
headline: Founding Director, USC Schaeffer Institute for Public Policy & Government Service · University Professor of Public Policy, Pharmacy, and Economics
about: Dana Goldman is University Professor of Public Policy, Pharmacy, and Economics and Founding Director of the Schaeffer Institute for Public Policy & Government Service at the University of Southern California. The Institute houses the Schaeffer Center for Health Policy & Economics, one of the most influential health economics programs in the world. He also serves as special advisor to the USC Provost and previously served as Dean of the USC Price School of Public Policy.

His research spans economics, medicine, and public policy — the economics of aging and longevity, prescription drug pricing and insurance design, and the value of medical innovation. He pioneered a “Netflix model” for paying for cures for the chronically ill, and has been awarded more than $150 million in research support from the National Institutes of Health, private industry, and philanthropy.

He has advised the Congressional Budget Office, the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine, Covered California, the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, GRAIL, Edwards Lifesciences, and the Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company. He is an elected member of the National Academy of Medicine, the National Academy of Social Insurance, and the National Academy of Public Administration, and a research associate at the National Bureau of Economic Research. From 2017 to 2025 he was a nonresident senior fellow at the Brookings Institution.

A committed mentor, he founded and led USC’s Resource Center for Minority Aging Research; past trainees are on the faculty at Stanford, Harvard, Duke, UCLA, UCSF, USC, Tufts, Penn, and Vanderbilt. He co-founded Precision Health Economics and EntityRisk. EntityRisk pairs health economics and policy expertise with PROVEN™, its machine-learning modeling platform, to help biopharmaceutical companies predict health outcomes, set value-based prices, and decide which evidence is worth generating.
